title: Maximum Average Subarray I
summary: You get a list of integers `nums` and an integer `k`. Among all subarrays made of k consecutive numbers in `nums`, find the one with the highest average and return that average. An answer within 10⁻⁵ of the exact value is accepted.

examples.explanation: The best subarray is [-1, 3, 8]. Its sum is 10, and 10 / 3 is about 3.33333.
Every pair has a negative sum. The best is [-6, -3], whose sum is -9, and -9 / 2 = -4.5.

constraints: −10⁴ ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10⁴, so numbers can be negative

approaches.twist: Slide a fixed window of k numbers, adding the one that enters and subtracting the one that leaves, and divide the best sum by k.
Add up every subarray of k consecutive numbers from scratch and keep the largest average.
approaches.note: Works, but summing each subarray from scratch takes O(n·k) time, which is O(n²) when k is about half of n. The target is O(n).

signals.meaning: The window has a fixed size, k: each step, one number enters on the right and one leaves on the left.
All candidates have the same length, so the highest average belongs to the highest sum. Track the sum, and divide by k once at the end.
The best sum can be below zero, so don't start it at 0. Start it at the first window's sum, or at float('-inf').

constraintReading: len(nums) can reach 10⁵, and k can be anything up to it. Summing each subarray from scratch costs O(n·k): about 2.5·10⁹ additions when k is half of n, which is O(n²) and far too slow. Aim for O(n) time and O(1) space by updating one sum as the window moves. Negative numbers are fine here, because the window's size never changes.

related.relation: Its window changes size, growing on the right and shrinking on the left while a letter repeats, instead of always holding k items.
